message.content:
In the Go repo at /bench/home/work (usememos/memos), answer two collision questions with exact path:line citations:

1. Find EVERY declaration of a method named RunOnce (grep `func (.*) RunOnce` across all .go files). For each declarer type, determine whether that RunOnce is invoked from production (non-test) code, and cite the caller path:line. Also check if RunOnce is invoked only from tests for some declarers.

2. Count every distinct declaration of a method named Close across backend Go code (grep `func (.*) Close(` in *.go, exclude web/). List the count and identify which types' Close methods are actually called by non-test server code (e.g., DB Close in server shutdown / main.go), citing caller path:line. Note: calls like `db.Close()` on *sql.DB are stdlib — distinguish repo-declared Close methods from stdlib ones; report which repo-declared Close declarations have production callers.

Return: (a) full list of RunOnce declarers with path:line, invoked-or-not, caller path:line; (b) count of Close declarations with list path:line, and which are invoked from non-test code with caller path:line.

attachment.content:
- graphify: Use for any question about a codebase, its architecture, file relationships, or project content — especially when graphify-out/ exists, where the question should be treated as a graphify query first. Turns any input (code, docs, papers, images, videos) into a persistent knowledge graph with god nodes, community detection, and query/path/explain tools.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

## (a) RunOnce declarations — 2 total

| # | Declarer | Declaration | Invoked from production? | Caller |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `*s3presign.Runner` | `/bench/home/work/server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:43` | **Yes** | `/bench/home/work/server/server.go:163` (`s3presignRunner.RunOnce(ctx)` in `Server.startBackgroundRunners`), plus internal production call from its own ticker loop at `/bench/home/work/server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:36` (`Run`) |
| 2 | `*memopayload.Runner` | `/bench/home/work/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:27` | **No — zero callers anywhere** | none (not production, not tests) |

Details:
- The `memopayload` package is imported only by `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:18`, and only its free function `RebuildMemoPayload` is used (`memo_service.go:108`, `memo_service.go:447`). `memopayload.NewRunner` and `(*Runner).RunOnce` are dead code — the `Runner` type is never constructed.
- No declarer has a *tests-only* RunOnce caller: `/bench/home/work/server/runner/s3presign/runner_test.go` contains no `RunOnce` reference (it exercises `CheckAndPresign`/other paths), so `s3presign` RunOnce is production-only, and `memopayload` RunOnce is uncalled.

## (b) Close declarations — 8 total in backend Go (web/ excluded)

Repo-declared:
1. `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go:99` — `func (h *SSEHub) Close()`
2. `/bench/home/work/store/db/sqlite/sqlite.go:67` — `func (d *DB) Close() error`
3. `/bench/home/work/store/db/mysql/mysql.go:47` — `func (d *DB) Close() error`

8. `/bench/home/work/store/test/filter_helpers_test.go:282` — `func (tc *AttachmentFilterTestContext) Close()` (test-only file)

Count: 8 declarations; 6 in production packages, 2 in `_test.go`.

### Which have non-test callers

| Declaration | Production caller |
|---|---|
| `*store.Store.Close` (`store/store.go:72`) | `/bench/home/work/server/server.go:146` — `if err := s.Store.Close(); err != nil {` inside `Server.Shutdown`, reached from `/bench/home/work/cmd/memos/main.go:101` (`s.Shutdown(ctx)`) |
| `*cache.Cache.Close` (`store/cache/cache.go:187`) | `/bench/home/work/store/store.go:74`, `:75`, `:76` (`instanceSettingCache`, `userCache`, `userSettingCache`) |
| sqlite `*DB.Close` (`store/db/sqlite/sqlite.go:67`) | `/bench/home/work/store/store.go:78` — `return s.driver.Close()` via the `Driver` interface (`/bench/home/work/store/driver.go:12`) |
| mysql `*DB.Close` (`store/db/mysql/mysql.go:47`) | same: `/bench/home/work/store/store.go:78` |
| postgres `*DB.Close` (`store/db/postgres/postgres.go:46`) | same: `/bench/home/work/store/store.go:78` |
| `*SSEHub.Close` (`server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go:99`) | `/bench/home/work/server/server.go:206` — `s.sseHub.Close()` in `Server.closeLongLivedConnections`, called from `Shutdown` (`server.go:141`) |
| `MemoFilterTestContext.Close` | tests only: `/bench/home/work/store/test/memo_filter_test.go` (many), `/bench/home/work/store/test/memo_filter_functions_test.go:16` etc. |
| `AttachmentFilterTestContext.Close` | tests only: `/bench/home/work/store/test/attachment_filter_test.go:18` etc. |

So all 6 non-test declarations have production callers; only the 2 test-context ones are test-exclusive.

### Stdlib vs repo-declared disambiguation

These `.Close()` call sites are **stdlib/third-party**, not repo declarations:
- `d.db.Close()` at `/bench/home/work/store/db/sqlite/sqlite.go:68`, `/bench/home/work/store/db/mysql/mysql.go:48`, `/bench/home/work/store/db/postgres/postgres.go:47` — these are `*sql.DB.Close` (the bodies of the repo-declared wrappers).
- `defer rows.Close()` (~60 sites across `store/db/{sqlite,mysql,postgres}/*.go`) — `*sql.Rows`.
- `resp.Body.Close()` / `response.Body.Close()` — `io.ReadCloser` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:156`, `internal/httpgetter/image.go:25`, `internal/httpgetter/html_meta.go:145`, `internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go:95`, `internal/storage/s3/s3.go:96`).

- `conn.Close()` in `proto/gen/api/v1/*.pb.gw.go` and `internal/email/client.go:90,124`, `writer.Close()` at `internal/email/client.go:168` — grpc/net/smtp stdlib.
- `file.Close()` / `reader.Close()` / `output.Close()` in `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` and `store/deployment_config.go:134` — `os.File` / `io.ReadCloser`.
- `server.Close()` in tests — `httptest.Server`.
